metadata.methods_description: Participants with implanted intracranial electrodes performed categorized free recall of 12-word lists drawn from 25 semantic categories. An L2 logistic regression classifier was trained on spectral power features (Morlet wavelets, 3-180 Hz) from 0-1366 ms after word onset in prior catFR1 sessions. It was validated with leave-one-session-out cross-validation and permutation testing. During stimulation lists, 500 ms stimulation was delivered to a single electrode when classifier output fell below a participant-specific Youden's J threshold. Each session comprised 26 lists, and the first 4 lists had no stimulation.

citation_details.title: Trematodes of Genera Gyrabascus and Parabascus from Bats in European Russia: Morphology and Molecular Phylogeny
citation_details.author: Nadezhda Yu. Kirillova, Sergei V. Shchenkov, Alexander Kirillov, Alexander B. Ruchin
citation_details.abstract: Morphological variability of trematodes from bats (Chiroptera) is poorly studied. Since the variability of adult digenean specimens may be rather high, morphological features are often insufficient for the identification of closely related species, and confirmation with the use of molecular data is required. The aim of our study was to combine the morphological and molecular phylogenetic analyses of several bat trematodes from the genera Gyrabascus and Parabascus (Pleurogenidae): Gyrabascus amphoraeformis, Gyrabascus oppositus, Parabascus lepidotus, Parabascus duboisi, and Parabascus semisquamosus, of which G. amphoraeformis and G. oppositus are little known in European Russia. We made detailed morphological descriptions of these trematodes from several definitive hosts, analyzed morphometric features, and generated new partial sequences of the 28S rRNA gene. A broad variability of trematodes of the genera Gyrabascus and Parabascus was revealed both from various host species and from specimens of the same host species. We propose a new taxonomic key for the identification of the studied species. Certain host specificity of these trematodes was revealed.
